children: By Robert Harvey and Marek Strzelecki

said on Wednesday it had bought 16 million barrels of extra oil for its Polish, Lithuanian and Czech plants, after traders said it was rushing to secure crude to cover disruptions to Saudi supplies until November.

Saudi Arabia's oil industry is grappling with the impact of a wave of attacks by Iran-aligned militia, including one which took its East-West Pipeline offline on September 10. State-owned Saudi Aramco
has been Orlen's largest oil supplier since 2022, providing around 40% of its volumes.

Orlen said in a statement on Wednesday that it had contracted 16 additional deliveries to its refineries in Poland, the Czech Republic and Lithuania, including from Norway, Great Britain, Algeria, Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan and the Americas.
Saudi Arabia has not said when its East-West Pipeline will re-open and market sources said Orlen is buying to cover demand for September and October.
Orlen issued two fresh tenders to buy crude oil on Wednesday, seeking North Sea grades in one and Brazilian or Guyanese crudes in the other, two physical oil traders said.
Orlen has in recent years weaned itself off Russian oil, which made up most of its crude intake around a decade ago.
Last month, it signed a deal with Norway's Equinor
for Sverdrup crude to cover 25% of its supply needs.

"The remaining part of the demand is covered, among others, on the basis of a contract concluded in August with Norway's Equinor," said Orlen, adding that it monitors the raw materials market situation and has a diversified supplier portfolio.
